name: James Hawkins
profile: British co-founder, with Tim Glaser, of PostHog, the open-source product-analytics and 'product OS' platform born in Y Combinator's W20 batch. PostHog has grown into session replay, feature flags, experiments, a data warehouse and AI tools, and claims 100,000+ customers. It has been cash-flow positive since Dec 2024, raised a Stripe-led $70M Series D (2025) and a $75M Series E (Oct 2025), and is valued at $1B+.
interesting_fact: PostHog says 54% of YC's first 2024 batch adopted it, making it one of the top three products used by YC companies. It is famous for an entirely public company handbook and a quirky hedgehog brand.
deep_cut_fact: PostHog's famous public handbook began as a hack. Before launching on Hacker News, Hawkins and Glaser wanted to 'look as mature as possible' with big footers like big, boring companies, so they wrote up how they wanted to work to fill the links.
notes: Very public, writes openly about running PostHog (handbook, newsletter, X), so a strong podcast candidate. The founders' first idea (Aug 2019) was a tool for managing technical debt, which failed before PostHog.

name: Naga Bharath Daka
profile: Former space scientist who co-founded Skyroot Aerospace in 2018 with CEO Pawan Kumar Chandana to make launches 'as routine as commercial air travel'. Skyroot launched India's first private rocket, Vikram-S, in 2022. Its Vikram-1 reached orbit on its first flight on 18 July 2026. The company has 1,000+ staff and has raised $160M at a $1.1B valuation from investors including GIC and Temasek.
interesting_fact: Skyroot's Vikram-1 lifted off from Sriharikota on 18 July 2026 and reached orbit on its maiden flight, India's first private orbital launch.
deep_cut_fact: Skyroot's hardware is named after Indian science greats: Raman-1, the first privately built rocket engine static-fired in India; Dhawan-1, India's first privately built cryogenic engine; the Kalam-250 stage; and the Vikram rockets.
notes: Hurun lists him as a founder of a $1B company; Skyroot itself states a $1.1B valuation. The co-founders are ex-ISRO scientists (from general reporting; Skyroot's page says 'space scientists-turned-entrepreneurs'). The tribute naming is our reading of the engine names, not stated explicitly on the page.
